product_overview: This backend service provides authenticated users with full lifecycle management for API keys, including creation, inspection, revocation, and regeneration. It uses Clerk for authentication, PostgreSQL for persistence, and Redis for supporting cached access patterns.
core_goals: Allow authenticated users to create and manage API keys securely
Enforce ownership and access control for all API key operations
Limit the number of active API keys per user to prevent abuse
Expose key metadata such as last-used timestamp without revealing secrets after creation
Support key regeneration and revocation workflows for credential rotation

features.name: API Key Listing
features.description: Authenticated users can retrieve a list of API keys that belong to their account.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/api-keys with a valid Clerk bearer token -> Receive 200 with an array of the user's API keys
GET /api/v1/api-keys without authentication -> Receive 401 Unauthorized response

features.name: API Key Creation
features.description: Authenticated users can create new API keys, subject to a maximum of five active keys.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/api-keys with a valid Clerk bearer token and available active-key slot -> Receive 201 with the plaintext API key shown once
POST /api/v1/api-keys with a valid Clerk bearer token after reaching five active keys -> Receive 400 Active-key limit exceeded
POST /api/v1/api-keys without authentication -> Receive 401 Unauthorized response

features.name: API Key Inspection
features.description: Authenticated users can inspect an API key to see its last-used timestamp.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/api-keys/:id with a valid Clerk bearer token for a key owned by the user -> Receive 200 with last_used_at metadata
GET /api/v1/api-keys/:id with no authentication or an invalid token -> Receive 401 Unauthorized response

features.name: API Key Revocation
features.description: Authenticated users can revoke an API key they own to prevent further use.
user_flows: DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/:id with a valid Clerk bearer token for a key owned by the user -> Receive 200 empty success response
DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/:id with no authentication or a key not owned by the user -> Receive 401 Unauthorized response

features.name: API Key Regeneration
features.description: Authenticated users can replace an existing owned API key with a newly generated secret for rotation purposes.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/api-keys/:id/regenerate with a valid Clerk bearer token for a key owned by the user -> Receive 201 with the new plaintext API key shown once
POST /api/v1/api-keys/:id/regenerate with no authentication or a key not owned by the user -> Receive 401 Unauthorized response

features.name: API Key Management
features.description: Authenticated users can create, list, revoke, inspect, and regenerate API keys.

endpoints.description: List API keys belonging to the authenticated user.
Create an API key for the authenticated user, limited to five active keys.

response_schema.201: Object containing the plaintext key once

endpoints.description: Retrieve the last-used timestamp for an API key.
Revoke an API key owned by the authenticated user.
Replace an owned API key with a newly generated secret.

response_schema.201: Object containing the new plaintext key once

known_limitations.issue: Production start script points to dist/main while Nest emits dist/src/main.js
known_limitations.impact: npm run start:prod fails unless the compiled entrypoint is started directly

known_limitations.issue: API key route authorization accepts either x-api-key or Clerk Bearer authentication
known_limitations.impact: Endpoint behavior depends on which authentication header is supplied

known_limitations.issue: Last-used lookup and revoke/regenerate authorization should be tested for ownership isolation
known_limitations.impact: Incorrect ownership handling could expose or modify another user's key
